title: 5 Geopolitical Scenarios — MOU Progress vs. Hormuz Permanence
hook: A 14-point MOU is on the table via Pakistani mediators. But Hormuz is closed for 69+ days, blockades persist on both sides, and the IRGC just seized a tanker. The tail risks are not symmetric.
authorWord: The market is pricing a 70% chance of deal — but the odds of a clean, comprehensive resolution are much lower. The most probable outcome is a fudge: extended ceasefire, partial Hormuz opening under Iranian conditions, and persistent risk premium. Think €40-50 for months.
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
🔥 BULL EXTREME — MOU Collapses, Full Escalation Resumes (15% prob): Iran rejects the MOU terms (Trump himself says he's "not satisfied"). IRGC escalates with another vessel seizure or direct attack on US mine-clearing operations in the Hormuz approach channel. The ceasefire formally collapses. Trump faces war powers deadline pressure and may escalate to force a resolution. TTF spikes to €65-80/MWh on the initial headline, with potential for €100+ if the Strait sees military escalation restricting all traffic. JKM surges past $25/MMBtu. Brent hits $120-130/bbl. Duration: weeks to months before any new ceasefire attempt.

💣 HIGH RISK — MOU Signed But Hormuz Remains Partially Closed (30% prob): The most likely path. Both sides agree to a ceasefire extension and framework MOU, but Iran insists on maintaining tolls and IRGC-coordinated passage. The US counter-blockade on Iranian ports persists. Commercial shipping gradually resumes but at 30-50% of pre-crisis volumes. Qatar begins partial Ras Laffan restarts (4-6 trains) with full restoration not expected before Q1 2027. TTF settles into a €42-52/MWh trading range with elevated volatility. LNG freight premium persists at $1-2/MMBtu above pre-crisis. Storage injection proceeds but at elevated cost. This scenario can persist for months — becoming the 'new normal' that the market slowly absorbs.

🔄 BASE CASE — Negotiations Drag Through Summer, Status Quo (30% prob): Talks continue via Pakistani mediators but progress is slow. Neither side makes meaningful concessions. Hormuz remains closed. Qatar cannot restart. EU storage continues filling with US and African LNG at elevated prices. TTF trades €44-50/MWh through summer with seasonal demand pickup pushing toward €55-60 in Q4. By October, if no deal is reached, the market prices in a winter with no Qatar LNG and below-target storage — potentially triggering emergency demand-reduction measures. The EU Gas Coordination Group activates Article 9 coordination. This is the slow-burn scenario.

⚓ MODERATE BULL — Comprehensive Deal, Full Hormuz Reopening (15% prob): Against expectations, the MOU is finalized with both sides agreeing to: (1) full Hormuz reopening under international monitoring, (2) removal of both blockades, (3) mutual ceasefire extension. QatarEnergy immediately begins Ras Laffan restart process. US Golden Pass and other new supply offsets the ramp-up period. TTF drops €5-8/MWh initially, then stabilizes at €38-42 as the market absorbs the Qatar restart timeline (end-August for full trains). The relief rally is front-loaded — by Q4, the market refocuses on winter fundamentals. This is the 'buy the rumor, sell the fact' scenario.

🔻 BEAR EXTREME — Deal + Rapid Reopening + Super El Niño Mild Winter (10% prob): The tail-bear scenario combines: (1) full MOU deal, (2) rapid Hormuz reopening within weeks, (3) Qatar accelerates Ras Laffan restart (training turbines from Asian facilities), (4) El Niño materializes as Super El Niño bringing mild NW European winter, and (5) Nordic hydro recovers faster than expected. TTF crashes to €30-35/MWh by autumn. The LNG freight premium collapses. JKM drops to $10-12/MMBtu. This scenario requires everything to break right — probability is low but not zero.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. TTF Iron Condor — Sell €38 Puts + Sell €55 Calls (Range Trade): With 60% probability assigned to the €42-52 range (Scenarios 2+3), selling an iron condor captures premium while defining risk. Sell Jun €38 puts at ~€0.50 and Jun €55 calls at ~€0.40. Buy €35 puts and €60 calls as wings for protection. Net credit ~€0.60-0.70. Max profit at expiry between €38-55. Max loss = €3.00-3.10 (wing width minus credit). Rationale: the market is stuck in a range until there's a binary outcome.

2. Long Dec '26 TTF / Short Jun '26 TTF (Calendar Risk Premium): Even if near-term resolution occurs, the winter 2026/27 contract must price in: (a) Qatar restart uncertainty, (b) storage deficit, (c) potential for renewed escalation. The Dec-Jun spread at ~€0 is too flat given these risks. Buy Dec '26, sell Jun '26. Target spread widening to €5-8. Stop if comprehensive deal is signed and Hormuz fully reopens.

3. Long TTF Jun '26 €45 Calls / Short €50 Calls (Bull Call Spread): For traders who think the base case (slow negotiations, status quo) supports modest upside from current €44. Buy €45 calls at ~€1.20, sell €50 calls at ~€0.80. Net cost ~€0.40. Max profit = €4.60 at €50. Max loss = €0.40. Reward/risk ratio of 11.5:1. The thesis: even without escalation, the market drifts higher as storage deficit becomes apparent through summer.

⚡ Dissenting View — Iris 🦋
Your probabilities sum to 100% but you're missing the 'muddle-through' scenario where Hormuz partially opens under Iranian conditions and stays that way indefinitely. That's not Scenario 2 (MOU signed) — it could happen without any MOU at all. Iran has every incentive to keep the strait under its control and collect tolls. The probability of 'no deal, partial opening, indefinite status quo' is higher than you think — maybe 20% on its own.
